page: Amazon Web Services x8g.12xlarge is an arm64-based server powered by 48 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Neoverse-V2 processor, running at 2.8 GHz. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, this instance features a 1:1 vCPU-to-physical-core ratio with no simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of memory, yielding 16.0 GB of RAM per core, which positions it as a memory-optimized resource. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this server type, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidth scoring in the top 10% tier. Passmark memory scores and database operations also rank in the top 10% tier. Multi-core CPU execution is robust, as shown by top 10% tier results in Geekbench multi-core and software compilation tests, alongside top 25% performance in stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench ray tracing. However, single-core capabilities are more moderate, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling in the middle 50% average category.

The high memory-to-core ratio provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring large in-memory datasets without the overhead of excessive CPU licensing. Tradeoffs include the lack of local NVMe storage and lower single-core performance compared to some x86 alternatives. Additionally, while text generation for medium-sized LLM models (7B) ranks in the top 25% tier, text generation for smaller models (135M) falls into the bottom 25% tier. This server is suited for database operations, in-memory caching systems like Redis, software compilation, and static web serving.
